newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy to see close to zero GDP growth Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Italy to see close to zero GDP growth Q1 1997.

text.p: Italy will see close to zero GDP growth in the first quarter of 1997 compared to the previous quarter, the chief economist of the state statistics institute ISTAT said on Wednesday.
Italy had a fall of 0.2 percent in GDP in the last quarter of 1996 compared to the previous quarter.
Enrico Giovannini also told reporters that he saw some sign of optimism for GDP growth in the second quarter of the year.
"It is probable that in the first quarter of 1997, growth will be near zero compared to the last quarter of of 1996," Giovannini told reporters at the presentation of ISTAT's annual report.
"Industry is negative and tourism is not going very well. There was big drop in tourism over Easter," he said.
"Businesses are starting to see a bit of optimism for the second quarter. There are some signs of optimism," he said.
"It would be a good result if we managed to reach 1.2 percent GDP this year," he said.
The government's official target for 1997 is for 1.2 percent growth -- Rome newsroom +396-6782501
